# House of Student raises $2 mn seed funding led by Saltwater Sutra, Nirmitsu Ventures
...
Founded by Vaibhav Verma, House of Student builds on the experience of Unilodgers, the student housing marketplace he previously founded. Student accommodation platform House of Student has raised $2 million in seed funding led by Saltwater Sutra and Nirmitsu Ventures, with participation from Gautam Verlekar, Bank of New York Mellon managing director Glen Fernandes, former UK India Business Council chief executive Richard McCallum, Singapore Gulf Bank executive vice-chairman Ali Moosa and other strategic investors.Existing investors from Unilodgers also participated in the round, which was a combination of equity and debt.

results.title: House of Student Raises $2 Mn Equity-Debt Seed — StartupFox
results.author: Sabyasachi Chandra
highlights:
House of Student, a student accommodation technology platform, has raised $2 million in a seed round structured as a combination of equity and debt. The round was co-led by Saltwater Sutra and Nirmitsu Inspirational Ventures, with participation from Gautam Verlekar, Glen Fernandes, Richard McCallum, Ali Moosa and existing investor Unilodgers. It was announced on 28 July 2026. The split between equity and debt has not been disclosed. Neither has the valuation, the dilution taken by the founder, the lender or the terms attached to the debt portion, whether the capital is released in tranches, or any revenue, booking volume or gross transaction value for the company. A debt component inside a seed round is not the same instrument as equity. It carries repayment obligations from a company that has published no revenue figure, and it does not convert into ownership. Without the split, the amount of equity capital actually raised is unknown, and so is the size of the balance sheet obligation created alongside it. House of Student said the capital will go towards product development, expanding housing supply, strengthening its artificial intelligence capabilities and supporting global expansion. That description comes from the company's press release. The company was founded in February 2025 by Vaibhav Verma and operates from Gurugram and the United States. It runs a platform for booking student accommodation and for managing housing networks, and says it plans to move into AI-enabled student support services. It claims more than 2.5 million verified student rooms across over 25 countries, including the United Kingdom, the United States, Australia, Canada, New Zealand, the UAE, Singapore and 18 European markets. Verma previously founded Unilodgers, which the company describes as the world's first student housing marketplace. The company also says Unilodgers was valued at $109 million in its first institutional round. Neither claim has been independently confirmed. House of Student competes with Uhomes, Amber and Uniplaces. The reporting on this round is thin. No filing, no financials and no independent confirmation of the operating claims are available at the time of writing.

results.title: Venture Capital News: House of Student, Soctera, Vaderis Therapeutics, H&MV Engineering - InfotechLead
results.author: Rajani Baburajan
highlights:
House of Student Raises $2 Million to Expand AI Housing Marketplace
...
House of Student has raised $2 million in seed funding through equity and debt to accelerate product development, AI capabilities and international expansion. Saltwater Sutra, a New York-Mumbai investment-banking group, led the financing alongside Nirmitsu Inspirational Ventures. Participants included Gautam Verlekar, Glen Fernandes, Richard McCallum, Ali Moosa and other strategic investors, while existing Unilodgers investors maintained their support. The San Francisco-based technology company operates a student-housing marketplace containing more than 2.5 million verified rooms across over 25 countries. Its coverage includes the United Kingdom, United States, Australia, Canada, New Zealand, United Arab Emirates, Singapore and 18 European nations. The capital will support platform improvements and broader market penetration as the company scales its global student-living marketplace and AI-driven services worldwide.
